units: dimensionless (0-100), one value per hydrologic soil group A/B/C/D
definition: SCS/NRCS runoff curve number: higher CN = more of a rain event becomes quick runoff, less infiltrates. Depends jointly on land cover/condition and hydrologic soil group (A = sandy, high infiltration; D = clayey, low infiltration). InVEST Seasonal Water Yield uses CN for the quickflow (event runoff) term.

how_to_estimate.summary: Cross your land-cover class (and its hydrologic condition) with the four hydrologic soil groups using an SCS CN table. Use a global tabulation (Asante et al. 2008 / GeoSFM, or Jaafar et al. 2019 / GCN250) where no national table exists. InVEST expects average antecedent runoff condition (ARC II).

methods.name: global operational CN table
methods.notes: CN by A-D for a coarse global land-cover legend; used in USGS FEWS NET continental hydrology.

methods.name: GCN250 class table (ARC II)
methods.notes: CN by A-D per ESA CCI land-cover class at 250 m; also gives dry (ARC I) and wet (ARC III) surfaces.

methods.name: national NRCS/TR-55 table
methods.notes: Preferred where it exists (e.g. USDA TR-55, national hydrology manuals).

how_to_choose: Pick the CN source whose land-cover class most closely matches yours in BOTH structure and hydrologic condition (poor/fair/good cover). FS28 chose per class: built/urban, cropland, irrigated land, shrubland, barren, mixed forest, evergreen broadleaf forest, herbaceous wetland and water from Asante et al. (2008); disturbed/fallow, dense hardwood and conifer plantations, and good-condition natural grassland from GCN250 (Jaafar et al. 2019). Keep CN_A < CN_B < CN_C < CN_D. Water = 98 in all groups. For infiltration-improving BMPs (cover crops, no-till, rotational grazing), lower CN by an absolute amount rather than changing the class.

records.caveats: For medium/low-density residential with gardens, a lower CN (open-space or 1/8-acre-lot rows in TR-55) is more appropriate.

by_source.livestock_area_bmp: lower CN by 18 units (absolute), representing ~+30% infiltration from multi-paddock / rotational grazing

context.study_area: FS28 BMP parameterisation; CN->infiltration curves computed per CN and rainfall depth then back-solved

records.caveats: Applied to the BMP class's CN_A..D. The source_key is nominal (CN method context); the reduction magnitudes are FS28 methodological choices backed by infiltration-increase literature (cover crops +34.8%, perennials +59.2%, multi-paddock grazing +29%). Verify for your soils.
